With 3 bidders and uniform value distribution on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to bid a fraction of my value to balance winning probability against profit margin. The theoretical optimal shading factor for n=3 bidders is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $46, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 of that to maximize expected profit while maintaining a competitive chance of winning against Andy and Charles.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n × value = (2/3)×35 ≈ 23.33. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while remaining competitive against two other rational bidders using similar strategies.
